title: Create and Import a Simulated Module
prompt: Write a module file named 'is_helpers.py' into the virtual filesystem containing a function format_sku(num) that returns f'SKU-{num:03d}'. Then import is_helpers and assign code = is_helpers.format_sku(7).
hints: Use with open('is_helpers.py', 'w') as f: to write the function definition.
solution:
with open('is_helpers.py', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write("def format_sku(num):\n    return f'SKU-{num:03d}'\n")

import importlib
import is_helpers
importlib.reload(is_helpers)
code = is_helpers.format_sku(7)
alternates:
with open('is_helpers.py', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write("def format_sku(num):\n    return f'SKU-{num:03d}'\n")

import importlib
import is_helpers
importlib.reload(is_helpers)
from is_helpers import format_sku
code = format_sku(7)
explanation: Any .py file on sys.path (including the current directory in Pyodide) can be imported as a module.

title: Modules and Environments Quiz
prompt: Check your understanding of venv and module shadowing.
solution: Q1: Isolate project dependencies; Q2: Shadows standard library
explanation: Virtual environments isolate dependencies, and local filenames can shadow stdlib modules.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of python -m venv .venv?
options: To isolate a project's installed packages from other projects
questions.explanation: venv creates an isolated Python environment per project.

questions.question: What happens if you name your script math.py and write import math inside it?
options: Python imports your own file instead of the standard library math module
questions.explanation: Because the current directory is first on sys.path, local files shadow stdlib modules with the same name.

title: __name__ == '__main__' guard
solution: Runs code only when executed directly, not when imported.
back: So the guarded block runs only when the file is executed directly, not when another file imports it.

title: sys.path purpose
solution: The list of directories Python searches when importing modules.
back: The list of directory paths Python searches in order when executing an `import` statement.
